newsitem.title: UK: Sleepy London precious metals in tight ranges.
newsitem.headline: Sleepy London precious metals in tight ranges.

text.p: Precious metal prices drifted within narrow price bands on Monday in quiet trading which was expected to continue ahead of the holidays, dealers said.
Gold was finding some support around $368 an ounce, but showed little enthusiam for breaking out of a tight range.
"With Christmas and New Year just around the corner, people aren't doing anything," one dealer said. "A $368-$370 range is probably as far as gold is going to go."
Bullion fixed at $368.25 an ounce, compared to $368.60 in the morning and $369.00 on Friday afternoon.
In New York's Comex futures market, February gold was down $0.20 from Friday's close, at $370.20 an ounce.
Prices had drifted slightly lower overnight as brokers squared their books ahead of the holidays and under pressure from a stronger dollar, dealers said.
Bullion traders said they were watching the equities market for direction. The Dow Jones index surged, then fell back in early U.S. trading.
But Friday's European Union pact on post-monetary union budget stability was having no apparent impact on the gold price so far, dealers said.
The prospect of European Monetary Union (EMU) has cast a bearish pall over the gold market in recent months amid uncertainty over gold's future role with European central banks.

Dealers are concerned that central banks may sell off some of their gold reserves in the rush to comply with EMU criteria. Some analysts said the stability pact would re-fuel optimism about the single currency project proceeding on schedule.
But rumours of sales by a central bank have already accompanied gold's sharp decline to three-year lows in recent weeks, analysts noted.

"The bad news is pretty well discounted," said analyst Andy Smith of Union Bank of Switzerland. "Whether (central banks) sell now or in two years, the market has already sold the rumour. This is cold coffee in a way."
The other precious metals were quiet and marginally lower, in tandem with gold.
Silver was down one cent at $4.81/$4.83, and seen trading in a tight trading range between $4.79 and $4.85 in the near term.
Platinum was $1.55 lower at $367.00/$368.00, while palladium was barely changed at $117.50/$118.50.
